interpretation.strong_true_process_recovery_claim: REFUTED in this frozen factorial: no truth was uniquely identifiable even with complete positive occurrence coverage.
interpretation.reason: Every truth case had at least one observationally equivalent or positive-state-superset false world, so positive occurrences supplied no witness capable of eliminating all alternatives.
interpretation.finite_world_falsification_claim: Conditionally supported: canonical cases show falsification when positive witnesses exist, while the factorial shows those witnesses need not exist.
interpretation.f4_note: The factorial did not contain a no-superset omitted-truth case, so the full two-sided F4 boundary was not exercised; only the survival branch was observed.

language_decision.recommendation: C++ backend is now permitted for larger sweeps, but first remove redundant repeated first-passage calculations in Python; keep Python as the audited reference implementation.
